13: /// ## What it does
14: /// Checks for commented-out Python code.
15: ///
16: /// ## Why is this bad?
17: /// Commented-out code is dead code, and is often included inadvertently.
18: /// It should be removed.
19: ///
20: /// ## Known problems
21: /// Prone to false positives when checking comments that resemble Python code,
22: /// but are not actually Python code ([#4845]).
23: ///
24: /// ## Example
25: /// ```python
26: /// # print("Hello, world!")
27: /// ```
28: ///
29: /// ## Options
30: /// - `lint.task-tags`
31: ///
32: /// [#4845]: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/4845

50: pub(crate) fn commented_out_code(
51:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
52:     locator: &Locator,
53:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
54:     settings: &LinterSettings,
55: ) {
56:     let mut comments = comment_ranges.into_iter().peekable();
57:     // Iterate over all comments in the document.
58:     while let Some(range) = comments.next() {
59:         let line = locator.line_str(range.start());
60: 
61:         if is_script_tag_start(line) {
62:             let line_end = locator.full_line_end(range.end());
63:             let rest = locator.after(line_end);
64:             let mut cursor = ScriptTagCursor::new(rest, line_end);
65:             let mut scanner = ScriptTagScanner {
66:                 script_start: range,
67:                 terminator: None,
68:             };
69:             if scanner.skip_script_comments(&mut comments, &mut cursor) {
70:                 continue;
71:             }
72:         }
73: 
74:         // Verify that the comment is on its own line, and that it contains code.
75:         if is_own_line_comment(line) && comment_contains_code(line, &settings.task_tags[..]) {
76:             let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(CommentedOutCode, range);
77:             diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::display_only_edit(Edit::range_deletion(
78:                 locator.full_lines_range(range),
79:             )));
80:             diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
81:         }
82:     }
83: }

90: impl ScriptTagScanner {
91:     /// Parses the rest of a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)
92:     /// script comment and moves `comments` past the script comment's end unless
93:     /// the script comment is invalid.
94:     ///
95:     /// Returns `true` if it is a valid script comment.
96:     fn skip_script_comments<I>(
97:         &mut self,
98:         comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>,
99:         cursor: &mut ScriptTagCursor<'_>,
100:     ) -> bool
101:     where
102:         I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,
103:     {
104:         while !cursor.text.is_empty() && cursor.offset < cursor.offset_back {
105:             cursor.line_start = cursor.offset;
106:             let remaining = cursor.text;
107:             let (line_with_ending, rest, ending_len) =
108:                 if let Some(position) = remaining.find(['\n', '\r']) {
109:                     let ending_len = if remaining.as_bytes()[position] == b'\r'
110:                         && remaining.as_bytes().get(position + 1) == Some(&b'\n')
111:                     {
112:                         2
113:                     } else {
114:                         1
115:                     };
116:                     let (line_with_ending, rest) = remaining.split_at(position + ending_len);
117:                     (line_with_ending, rest, ending_len)
118:                 } else {
119:                     (remaining, "", 0)
120:                 };
121:             cursor.text = rest;
122:             cursor.line_end = cursor.line_start + line_with_ending.text_len();
123:             cursor.offset = cursor.line_end;
124: 
125:             let line = &line_with_ending[..line_with_ending.len() - ending_len];
126:             let Some(content) = script_tag_line_body(line) else {
127:                 break;
128:             };
129: 
130:             if content == "///" {
131:                 // > Precedence for an ending line # /// is given when the next line is not a valid
132:                 // > embedded content line as described above.
133:                 // > For example, the following is a single fully valid block:
134:                 // > ```python
135:                 // > # /// some-toml
136:                 // > # embedded-csharp = """
137:                 // > # /// <summary>
138:                 // > # /// text
139:                 // > # ///
140:                 // > # /// </summary>
141:                 // > # public class MyClass { }
142:                 // > # """
143:                 // > # ///
144:                 // ````
145:                 let terminator = cursor.line_end;
146:                 if next_line_is_script_tag(cursor) {
147:                     continue;
148:                 }
149:                 self.terminator = Some(terminator);
150:                 break;
151:             }
152:         }
153: 
154:         // > Unclosed blocks MUST be ignored.
155:         let Some(end_offset) = self.terminator else {
156:             return false;
157:         };
158: 
159:         // Skip over all script-comments.
160:         while let Some(comment) = comments.peek() {
161:             if comment.start() >= end_offset || comment.start() < self.script_start.start() {
162:                 break;
163:             }
164: 
165:             comments.next();
166:         }
167: 
168:         true
169:     }
170: }

174:         return false;
175:     }
176: 
177:     cursor.line_start = cursor.offset;

196:     let line = &line_with_ending[..line_with_ending.len() - ending_len];

209:         }
210:         if !char.is_whitespace() {
211:             return false;
212:         }
213:     }
214:     unreachable!("Comment should contain '#' character")
215: }

6: /// Cursor over the remaining source of a PEP 723 script comment block.
7: pub(crate) struct ScriptTagCursor<'a> {

9:     pub(crate) offset: TextSize,
10:     pub(crate) offset_back: TextSize,
11:     pub(crate) line_start: TextSize,

15: impl<'a> ScriptTagCursor<'a> {
16:     pub(crate) fn new(text: &'a str, offset: TextSize) -> Self {
17:         let text_len = text.text_len();
18:         Self {
19:             text,
20:             offset,
21:             offset_back: offset + text_len,
22:             line_start: offset,
23:             line_end: offset,
24:         }
25:     }
26: }

28: /// Returns the body of a PEP 723 embedded content line, if `line` is a valid
29: /// script-comment line.
30: pub(crate) fn script_tag_line_body(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
31:     let mut cursor = Cursor::new(line);
32:     if !cursor.eat_char('#') {
33:         return None;
34:     }
35:     if cursor.is_eof() {
36:         return Some("");
37:     }
38:     if !cursor.eat_char(' ') {
39:         return None;
40:     }
41:     Some(cursor.as_str())
42: }

part.text: The rule already recognizes metadata blocks, but its PEP 723 terminator-precedence scan treats subsequent ordinary `#` comments as embedded metadata, invalidates the block, and then falls back to ERA001. I’ll adjust the ERA001-specific traversal so the recognized metadata’s initial closing delimiter still protects the block.
